question.problem:
Consider the function $y=6{x}^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=6{x}^{x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=6{x}^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(6{x}^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡6+\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡6+x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡6+x\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)}^{′}+(x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+(x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =0+1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x+x\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=6{x}^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =6{x}^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1$
